subject: The Papyrus · Egypt's biggest earner isn't the Suez Canal
html:
The economy runs on love, not just ships

Ask what brings the most foreign currency into Egypt and most people say the Suez Canal, or tourism, or oil. The real answer: the money Egyptians working abroad send home to their families. In 2024 that was about $29.6 billion — making Egypt one of the world's top-ten remittance recipients, and dwarfing net foreign investment (roughly 3–5 times larger). (Source: World Bank.)

A crash that never happened

Now the data-literacy twist. Remittances hit a record $31.5bn in 2021, then appear to collapse to $19.5bn in 2023. A disaster? No — Egyptians abroad didn't suddenly earn a third less. During the currency crisis they routed money through the parallel (black-market) exchange to get more pounds per dollar, so it vanished from the official channel the statistics count. After the March-2024 float made the official rate competitive again, it reappeared at $29.6bn. The money never left; only the pipe it flowed through changed. (Source: World Bank; the note flags that even the 2024 figure is disputed, ~$29.6bn vs ~$22.7bn.)

That's the whole lesson: a number can fall off a cliff while the reality behind it barely moves. If you only read the headline figure, you'd have called a crisis that wasn't there. If you know how the number is collected, you see the real story — which is exactly what querying data yourself teaches you.

An economy held up, in large part, by people who left. See you next month.
